options.b: Lipids rarely switch leaflets without enzymes such as flippases
options.c: Flippases move cholesterol into the glycocalyx
options.d: The two leaflets always have identical composition

options.a: Sugars on the outer membrane surface that help cells recognize one another
options.b: The inner layer of water-avoiding tails
options.c: A type of cholesterol molecule
options.d: An enzyme that flips lipids between leaflets

questions.prompt: Which role is supported for the glycocalyx?

options.a: Setting the composition of each leaflet
options.b: Restraining fluid movement in the cold
options.c: Lowering the chain length of fatty acid tails
options.d: Distinguishing self from non-self

answer_key.rationale: Phospholipid heads are water-loving and face water on both sides, while the water-avoiding tails are tucked inside the bilayer.
Double bonds kink unsaturated tails, making close packing harder and increasing membrane fluidity.
Saturated tails pack closely, while kinked unsaturated tails pack less closely, allowing more movement and higher fluidity.
The explanation lists tail saturation, chain length, temperature, and cholesterol as factors affecting membrane fluidity.
Cholesterol restrains movement when the membrane is very fluid, buffering fluidity rather than increasing it.
Cholesterol prevents excessive stiffening of the membrane in the cold, which is part of its buffering role.
The fluid mosaic model describes a mixture of lipids, cholesterol, and proteins whose components can move sideways.
The explanation says lipids rarely switch leaflets without enzymes such as flippases, floppases, and scramblases.
The glycocalyx is formed by sugars on the outer surface and helps cells recognize one another.
The explanation says the glycocalyx helps cells recognize one another, including distinguishing self from non-self.

payload.explanation_text: A cell membrane is a flexible boundary. Phospholipids have water-loving heads and water-avoiding tails: this combination is called amphipathic. They form a bilayer with heads toward water on both sides and tails tucked inside. Saturated fatty acid tails pack closely. Double bonds kink unsaturated tails, making close packing harder and increasing fluidity. Fluidity describes how freely membrane components move. Tail saturation, chain length, temperature, and cholesterol affect it. Cholesterol buffers fluidity: it restrains movement when the membrane is very fluid and prevents excessive stiffening in the cold. The fluid mosaic model describes a mixture of lipids, cholesterol, and proteins whose components can move sideways. The two membrane layers, or leaflets, differ in composition. Lipids rarely switch leaflets without enzymes such as flippases, floppases, and scramblases. Sugars on the outer surface form the glycocalyx and help cells recognize one another, including distinguishing self from non-self.

concepts.name: Amphipathic phospholipids form the bilayer
concepts.taught_summary: Amphipathic phospholipids form a bilayer: water-loving heads face water on both sides; water-avoiding tails face inward.

concepts.name: Saturated vs. unsaturated fatty acids
concepts.taught_summary: Saturated tails pack closely; double bonds kink unsaturated tails, hindering close packing and increasing fluidity.

concepts.name: What affects membrane fluidity
concepts.taught_summary: Membrane fluidity is affected by tail saturation, chain length, temperature, and cholesterol.

concepts.name: Cholesterol as a fluidity buffer
concepts.taught_summary: Cholesterol restrains movement in a very fluid membrane and prevents excessive stiffening in the cold.

concepts.name: Fluid mosaic model
concepts.taught_summary: The fluid mosaic model describes lipids, cholesterol, and proteins with components able to move sideways.

concepts.name: Membrane asymmetry and lipid flipping
concepts.taught_summary: Leaflets differ in composition; switching leaflets is rare without flippases, floppases, or scramblases.

concepts.name: Glycocalyx and cell recognition
concepts.taught_summary: Outer-surface sugars form the glycocalyx and support cell recognition and self/non-self distinction.
